summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted for worsening lower extremity edema in the setting of chronic lymphedema, morbid obesity, and recurrent cellulitis. She presented with increased swelling up to her thighs, shortness of breath on exertion, and concern for possible cellulitis in the right foot. Initial labs showed leukocytosis and normal BNP, with a clear chest X-ray, ruling out acute heart failure. She was treated with IV furosemide, adjusted for rising creatinine, and a short course of IV clindamycin for possible cellulitis, later discontinued due to lack of improvement. A transient neurologic event was evaluated by neurology and attributed to factors including volume status and sedating medications, with a normal Keppra level. Gabapentin was started for neuropathic pain, and nystatin for oral thrush. She stabilized with improved edema, continued home medications, and was discharged home with home health services and follow-up plans.
problems: Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Elevated white blood cell count, unspecified
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other organs and systems
